_: The standings registry, v2 (results-lifecycle policy, decision 92; scenario redesign, decision 103). One entry per published perf/quality axis: the current-standings file (null until the axis has been measured), the single sha its rows were measured at, the release it was refreshed for, and `plane` (cpu or gpu), the source set whose digest decides whether the axis is still current. Every axis also carries hash_set (its plane's digest at refresh time) and refs (reference-library versions measured against), which let scripts/check_standings.py's release gate skip a refresh when neither has moved, and let `--stale` tell the refresh driver which axes a session must actually measure. Gates: scripts/check_standings.py; supersession is in place, git history is the archive.

carried_forward.reason: Host CPU-fill changes moved the plane digest but cannot reach the device plane. src/cuda and include/bonsai/cuda are byte-identical between this axis's measured commit and the stamped one, verified for both 148f21b and 4fd9531, whose src/ and include/ trees are themselves identical to each other. Every GPU spec pins its thread count, so the auto-path cgroup quota clamp cannot apply either. Byte identity is not available as proof on this plane because device accumulation order varies run to run, so equivalence is argued against the measured noise floor: cross-commit prediction deltas at 148f21b versus f078f51 sit at the same magnitude as run-to-run deltas within either commit. Measured on cuda_depthwise, the tighter arm and the one recorded here, and on cuda_leafwise, whose deltas were identical within and across commits. cuda_levelwise shares the level-batched path and was not measured directly.
